title: SDK integration walkthrough - Cobalt Payments
summary: Redwood AE and SE walked Cobalt Payments through SDK quickstarts for Python and TypeScript, auth options (API key vs SSO), env setup for hosted vs private, and sample integration patterns. Customer is evaluating hosted API first with plan to test Dedicated for high-volume routing. Next steps: share quickstart links, pricing, and a short benchmark plan.
next_steps: Maya: Send Python/TS quickstart repos and example apps (by 2026-09-09)
Diego: Share internal benchmark checklist and suggested prompt set (by 2026-09-10)
Samir: Confirm pilot scope and expected QPS for Dedicated evaluation (by 2026-09-13)
Priya: Provide list of compliance docs needed (SOC2 papers)
action_items: Maya Patel: Email quickstart links + security docs - due 2026-09-09
Diego Ruiz: Provide benchmark template + sample scripts - due 2026-09-10
Priya Nair: Share target latency SLOs and pilot QPS - due 2026-09-13
transcript:
00:00 - Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Maya from Redwood Inference, and with me is Diego, our solutions engineer. Good to meet you Samir, Priya.
00:06 - Samir: Hey thanks Maya, appreciate it. We wanted a practical walkthrough today, specifically Python + TypeScript SDKs, auth setup, and how quickly we can get a test up and running.
00:12 - Priya: And also curious about hosted vs Dedicated and the V P C onboarding path.
00:18 - Diego: Great yeah we'll cover those. Quick agenda: install quickstarts, set env vars, run a sample request, and then cover auth (API keys, SSO), and then ops stuff like streaming, batching and cost controls.
00:27 - Maya: We won't go too deep into pricing but we'll outline next steps.
00:35 - Diego: Ok let's start with Python. The package name is redwood-inference, you can pip install redwood-inference. Example, in terminal: pip install redwood-inference, then set REDWOOD_API_KEY as an env var.
01:02 - Priya: Is that the same key for hosted and dedicated?
01:05 - Diego: For hosted yes, your API key scopes access to your account. For Dedicated/Private you typically get a different key or TLS mTLS certs depending on the deployment; we'll walk that flow later.
01:14 - Samir: Any SSO support for team-level credentials?
01:17 - Maya: Yes, SSO via SAML/OKTA for Console access, and for programmatic access you can mint service keys via the Console with RBAC. We have audit logs and key rotation built into the Console.
01:28 - Diego: Back to the quickstart, sample Python snippet: client = Redwood(api_key=os.getenv('REDWOOD_API_KEY')) then client.generate("your prompt") — streaming supported with a .stream() call.
01:44 - Priya: Sounds straightforward. For TypeScript is it @redwood/inference on npm?
01:47 - Diego: Exactly, npm i @redwood/inference, and usage is similar: const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY }); await client.generate({ model: 'rwd-3-quant', prompt: '...' });
02:06 - Samir: You mentioned rwd-3-quant, do you recommend quantized models by default?
02:10 - Diego: For cost-sensitive workloads yes, quantized models give good latency/cost tradeoffs. For worst-case quality-critical generation we suggest evals first; Redwood Optimize gives profiling and quantization suggestions automatically.
02:21 - Priya: How do we configure batching? We have bursty traffic at checkout times.
02:25 - Diego: On hosted we have automatic batching with per-route knobs. In Dedicated you can set batching window and max batch size in the runtime config. There's also prefix caching / KV cache that helps for repeated context.
02:38 - Samir: KV cache — is that safe for PII?
02:41 - Maya: You control cache retention and whether it's enabled per route. For regulated data you can disable caching, or use Private where logs and cache storage is customer-controlled.
02:50 - Priya: For VPC/Private, how long does onboarding take?
02:53 - Maya: Typical VPC onboarding is 2-4 weeks depending on network approvals. On-prem air-gapped is longer; we provide an install bundle and runbook. For Dedicated inside a cloud VPC we can usually stand up within a week if the infra team is ready.
03:06 - Diego: I'll show a short TypeScript demo now. Sharing screen... so here's the repo: github.com/redwood-ai/quickstarts/sdk-ts, inside src/index.ts. First you export REDWOOD_API_KEY in your .env, then run npm run dev, it calls the SDK and prints streaming tokens.
03:24 - Diego: Note on streaming — client.stream() gives partial tokens, useful for UI responses. For server-to-server you can also use chunked transfer and we support SSE and websockets.
03:35 - Samir: Any rate limits on streaming?
03:38 - Diego: Rate limits apply by tokens per minute and concurrent connections; we surface quotas in Console. For Dedicated you get negotiated throughput.
03:47 - Priya: For auth, can we use a short-lived token from our auth server?
03:51 - Maya: Yes you can create ephemeral tokens via the Console API; those tokens are short lived and can be minted by your identity provider. Works well with SSO.
04:01 - Diego: Ok next: environment variables and config. We recommend keeping keys in a secrets manager and injecting at runtime. For local dev a .env is fine. Example env: REDWOOD_API_KEY, REDWOOD_BASE_URL (for private endpoints), REDWOOD_REGION.
04:18 - Priya: For Private the base url will be internal like https://inference.internal.cobalt.
04:22 - Diego: Correct. Also for mTLS you can configure client certs and the SDK supports a cert path option.
04:28 - Samir: How do logs and observability look?
04:30 - Maya: Console shows per-route latencies, token-level cost, error traces, and retentions. You can send traces to Datadog or export logs via S3. For GDPR we support data deletion APIs.
04:43 - Diego: Also important: Redwood Optimize — after a few thousand requests it will suggest batching levels, model variants, and quantization profiles to reduce cost. We can share example reports.
04:54 - Priya: Nice. Ok can you show a minimal python end-to-end?
04:57 - Diego: Sure. On screen: virtualenv, pip install redwood-inference, set REDWOOD_API_KEY, run python example.py. Example prints returned text, and shows streaming in chunks. Watch for slight hesitation while the client warms up — that's the KV cache warming and model seeding.
05:15 - Samir: Is there SDK telemetry we need to be aware of?
05:18 - Maya: The SDK emits basic telemetry for debugging (latency, errors) but no request payloads by default. You can opt in or disable telemetry via env.
05:27 - Priya: We need SOC2 docs for procurement.
05:29 - Maya: We'll attach SOC2 and penetration test summary in the follow-up email.
05:33 - Diego: Quick question — what's your pilot traffic like in terms of QPS and average tokens per request?
05:38 - Samir: We're targeting 50 rps at peak and average 120 tokens per request for the first pilot. Could go up over time to 300 rps.
05:46 - Diego: Great, that's in range for a Dedicated evaluation. For Hosted we can usually accommodate initial pilots but Dedicated gives predictable throughput and cost. We'll propose both paths.
05:56 - Priya: For prompt storage, do you recommend storing prompts on our side or in Redwood?
05:59 - Maya: Best practice is to keep user PII on your side and only send what's needed to Redwood. For templates you can store them in Redwood as templates but set retention and RBAC.
06:12 - Samir: Any gotchas on the TypeScript client bundling?
06:15 - Diego: SSR and client bundles should not include API keys. For serverless functions, keep key in env and call from server. We have an example for Vercel and AWS Lambda.
06:25 - Priya: Can we do tool/function calling with the SDK?
06:27 - Diego: Yes, function calling is supported. In TypeScript you register a function schema and Redwood routes structured outputs. We did mention earlier that parser sometimes transcribes 'function calling' oddly in older docs, but the SDK supports it.
06:38 - Samir: Unit testing — any recommendations?
06:40 - Diego: We recommend mocking the client in unit tests and using local deterministic responses for CI. For integration tests you can use a staging key and a small model to keep costs predictable.
06:51 - Priya: For the Console, how do rollouts work?
06:54 - Maya: You can do canary rollouts by traffic percentage, A/B tests with route-level flags, and automatic fallback policies in case of latency spikes.
07:05 - Samir: Ok great. Can you outline the pilot steps?
07:08 - Maya: Step 1: Send quickstart repos and security docs. Step 2: Cobalt runs a 2-week hosted pilot using a sample prompt set. Step 3: Run benchmark scripts Diego will provide to capture latency and token costs. Step 4: Evaluate results and if traffic pattern demands, spin up Dedicated or Private.
07:25 - Diego: I'll share a benchmark checklist that captures p95, p99 latencies, tokens/request, concurrency, and tails.
07:32 - Priya: On SLA — what are uptime and latency SLOs for Dedicated?
07:35 - Maya: Dedicated comes with SLA options; typical is 99.9% uptime and negotiated latency SLOs based on model class. We'll surface those in the contract.
07:44 - Samir: Any examples of customers in payments?
07:47 - Maya: We run with a few payments and fraud detection customers, names shared in case studies. (slight crosstalk)
07:55 - Diego: Quick demo wrap-up: here's a live run of a sample TypeScript app calling a reranker endpoint. It shows how to call embeddings, store vectors, and rerank results. Note that embeddings are billed differently and we show token breakdown in the Console.
08:15 - Priya: For encryption keys, can we bring our own KMS?
08:18 - Maya: Yes, BYOK via KMS/HSM for Private and Dedicated. Hosted supports CMKs for enterprise plans. We'll include config docs.
08:26 - Samir: Anything else we should be aware of for compliance?
08:29 - Maya: We have audit logs, SSO, RBAC, encryption at rest and in transit. For regulated PII flows we'd recommend Private deployment.
08:38 - Diego: Ok one more note on dev ergonomics: we have codegen snippets in the Console for Python, TS, and cURL so your devs can copy paste.
08:47 - Priya: Great, that will speed onboarding.
08:50 - Maya: Quick recap and next steps — we'll send the quickstarts, SOC2, benchmark checklist, and a pricing/commit sketch for Dedicated.
08:59 - Samir: Awesome, thanks.
09:01 - Maya: Thanks everyone, we'll follow up by email with items Diego just mentioned.
09:05 - Diego: I'll attach the sample prompt set and benchmark scripts.
09:08 - Priya: Thanks, bye.
09:10 - [call ended]
file_notes: Transcript contains minor transcription artifacts: 'V P C' spelled out, 'K V cache' for KV cache, occasional missing punctuation consistent with automated transcripts.
